name: The Nation cryptic crossword No 3260
preamble: Joshua Kosman and Henri Picciotto Share Copy Link Facebook X (Twitter) Bluesky Pocket Email November 7, 2012 This article appears in the November 26, 2012 issue.

clue.text: Gingrich returns, superficially trustworthy and clear-sighted

indicators.note: something that returns comes back the way it went, so the name is read from right to left
on the surface only, so just the outside letters of the following word are kept

blocks.note: Newt Gingrich, the former US Speaker of the House
the first and last letters of the word
the same name again, seen a second time through double vision
the same outer letters again, seen a second time

explanation.surface: A politician comes back looking honest and sharp-eyed, at least on the surface.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the seven double-vision clues: the wordplay builds TWENTY, and seeing it twice gives TWENTY-TWENTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Twenty-twenty is the standard score for normal visual acuity, so it describes perfect eyesight or clear insight.

clue.text: Rum drunk during work leads to disruption

indicators.note: someone drunk staggers about unsteadily, so these letters lurch into a new order
during means in the course of, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: toil is hard work
the letters of rum rearranged

explanation.surface: Drinking rum on the job causes chaos at the workplace.
explanation.definitionFit: Turmoil is a state of great confusion or upheaval, which is what disruption brings.

clue.text: Pass or shuffle, please

indicators.note: shuffling cards mixes their order, so these letters are mixed too

blocks.note: the letters to be mixed

explanation.surface: A card player asks to be allowed to pass or to mix the deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass' and 'shuffle' both sound like card-table moves; only 'Pass' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: When time passes it elapses, so the two verbs are synonyms for time going by.

clue.text: Carry to Tallahassee's outskirts

indicators.note: the outskirts of a town are its edges, so only the outer letters are taken

blocks.note: taken as written
the first and last letters of Tallahassee

explanation.surface: Hauling something out to the edge of Florida's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Tallahassee is the state capital of Florida; only its two edge letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: To tote is an informal American verb for carrying something, as with a tote bag.

clue.text: First of ten, approximately, in trunk

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is taken

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
or so means roughly, as in ten or so

explanation.surface: Roughly the first ten of something packed in a storage chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trunk' suggests luggage or an elephant, but here it means the body.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the trunk of the human body, without the head and limbs.

clue.text: Farm animals mounting male in tangled webs

indicators.note: a tangled thread is twisted out of order, so these letters are twisted into a new one

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Livestock clambering onto a ram and getting caught up in netting.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a racy farmyard image; male and webs together are mixed into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ewe lambs are young female sheep, kept on farms for breeding.

clue.text: Newspaper, a bit old, is recycled

indicators.note: recycled material is broken down and made into something new, so these letters are remade

blocks.note: the three words supply the letters

explanation.surface: Yesterday's paper, a little stale, goes off to the recycling bin.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabloid is a newspaper with small pages, often popular and sensational in style.

clue.text: Dog food

blocks.note: first meaning: a fluffy Chinese breed with a blue-black tongue
second meaning: seen twice, the slang word for food doubled

explanation.walkthrough: A double-vision clue: chow is slang for food, and seeing 'food' twice gives the dog breed's doubled name.
explanation.definitionFit: The chow chow is a Chinese breed of dog, and chow is informal American slang for something to eat.

clue.text: Callas doesn't begin operatic excerpt

indicators.note: a word that doesn't begin is missing its opening letter

blocks.note: Maria Callas, the opera soprano

explanation.surface: The great soprano fails to start her operatic showpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: The surname leads you to her first name, which loses its M.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo song from an opera, often performed on its own as a concert piece.

clue.text: Revolutionary: "Free Earth from now on!"

indicators.note: a revolution overturns the existing order, so these letters are turned over into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the two words supply the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A revolutionary's slogan promises to liberate the planet starting today.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like the speaker of the slogan, but it only signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereafter is a formal adverb meaning in future, from this point onward.

clue.text: Spill beer around, beginning to mine for coal after a fire

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is taken
spilt liquid ends up in a jumbled mess, so these letters are scattered into a new order
around says one piece wraps itself about the other

blocks.note: the letters of beer rearranged
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone knocks over a pint and starts digging for fuel after a blaze.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled beer is split around the M: E, then M, then BER.
explanation.definitionFit: An ember is a glowing lump of coal or wood left smouldering once a fire dies down.

clue.text: Tiger-like, or evoking the forest

blocks.note: Tiger Woods, the golfer
the suffix -y makes an adjective meaning like or resembling

explanation.surface: Describing something as either catlike and striped or redolent of the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tiger-like' pulls toward the big cat, but the tiger is the golfer, and -like becomes the adjective ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Woodsy is an American adjective for things suggestive of woodland, like a woodsy scent.

clue.text: Island to the west — a steal

indicators.note: in an across entry, heading west means travelling right to left, so the words are read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
to steal is to rob
taken as written, seen a second time through double vision
the same synonym again, seen a second time

explanation.surface: An island lying westward is offered at a bargain price.
explanation.walkthrough: A double-vision clue: the wordplay gives BORA, and seeing it twice gives the island BORA-BORA in French Polynesia.
explanation.definitionFit: Bora-Bora is a Pacific island in the Society group of French Polynesia, famous for its lagoon resorts.

clue.text: Musical instrument in A (though getting higher)

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means reading from the bottom up, so the word is turned backwards

blocks.note: but and though both introduce a contrast
taken as written

explanation.surface: A musical instrument pitched in the key of A, though tuned upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In A' reads like a key signature; the A is just a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The tuba is the large, low-pitched brass instrument of a band or orchestra.

clue.text: Stop snake leaving pavement

indicators.note: when something leaves, it is no longer there, so those letters are taken out of the word

blocks.note: the asp is a small venomous snake
asphalt is a road or pavement surface

explanation.surface: An order to halt a snake as it slithers off the sidewalk.
explanation.walkthrough: Take ASP from the front of ASPHALT and HALT remains.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt is to come to a stop or bring something to a standstill.

clue.text: Holly is friendly

blocks.note: Buddy Holly, the rock and roll singer
the same first name again, seen a second time through double vision

explanation.surface: A short statement that someone called Holly is a sociable sort.
explanation.walkthrough: A double-vision clue: Holly's first name is Buddy, and seeing it twice gives BUDDY-BUDDY.
explanation.definitionFit: Buddy-buddy is an informal American adjective for very chummy or overly familiar.

clue.text: Jackass is told off

indicators.note: something off is wrong or out of order, so these letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A fool gets a telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Told off' reads as a single phrase for a scolding, but 'off' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A jackass, in the insulting sense, is a stupid person, which is what a dolt is.

clue.text: Doris brought up a bunch of empty verbiage

indicators.note: in a down entry, bringing something up means reading it from the bottom, so the name is backwards

blocks.note: Doris Day, the singer and film star
taken as written
the same surname again, seen a second time through double vision
taken as written, seen a second time

explanation.surface: Someone named Doris raises a heap of meaningless talk.
explanation.walkthrough: A double-vision clue: DAY reversed plus A gives YADA, and seeing it twice gives YADA YADA.
explanation.definitionFit: Yada yada is American slang for boring, predictable chatter, a stretch of talk with nothing in it.

clue.text: Dance beat for Indians, perhaps

blocks.note: a ball is a formal dance
to club is to beat with a stick

explanation.surface: A drumbeat to accompany dancing for Native Americans.
explanation.walkthrough: The Indians are the Cleveland Indians, the baseball team (since renamed the Guardians); 'perhaps' marks them as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball club is a professional baseball team, and the Cleveland Indians were one.

clue.text: Everything can be found in Washington city

indicators.note: found in says one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: WA is the postal abbreviation for Washington state
everything is all of it
the same abbreviation again, seen a second time through double vision
the same synonym again, seen a second time

explanation.surface: A boast that a certain city in Washington stocks every possible thing.
explanation.walkthrough: A double-vision clue: ALL in WA gives WALLA, and seeing it twice gives the city WALLA WALLA. 'Washington' does double duty, in the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Walla Walla is a city in southeastern Washington state, known for its sweet onions and wineries.

clue.text: Silence maintained by crazy loon in the distant past

indicators.note: something crazy is all over the place, so these letters are thrown into a new order
maintained by says one piece is held and supported inside the other

blocks.note: the letters of loon rearranged
a gag silences someone

explanation.surface: A madman kept quiet back in olden days.
explanation.definitionFit: Long ago is an adverb phrase for a time far back in history.

clue.text: Engulfed by existential question, start to despair

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is used

blocks.note: Am I? is the basic question of existence
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A philosopher swamped by the question of their own being begins to lose hope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engulfed by' looks like an instruction to put one piece inside another, but it is the definition; the pieces simply follow each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Amid is a preposition meaning in the middle of or surrounded by, which is what engulfed by describes.

clue.text: Wet some tin haphazardly

indicators.note: done haphazardly means without order or plan, so the letters fall in a random order

blocks.note: the two words supply the letters

explanation.surface: Splashing water carelessly over a few cans.
explanation.definitionFit: To moisten is to make slightly damp, which is a way to wet something.

clue.text: Arab: "The old nickel captivated me"

indicators.note: to captivate is to take captive, so one piece is held inside the other

blocks.note: ye is an archaic spelling of the
Ni is the chemical symbol for nickel
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Arab speaker confesses to being charmed by an antique coin.
explanation.walkthrough: The old and nickel together make YENI, which then holds ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yemeni is a person from Yemen, an Arab country on the southern tip of the Arabian Peninsula.

clue.text: Chinese pianist's nonstandard speech: omitting the first letter

indicators.note: omitting means leaving out, and the first letter is the one dropped from the front

blocks.note: slang is informal, nonstandard language

explanation.surface: A comment on how a Chinese pianist talks, with an odd remark about a missing letter.
explanation.walkthrough: A double-vision clue: SLANG without its S gives LANG, and seeing it twice gives LANG LANG.
explanation.definitionFit: Lang Lang is a famous concert pianist from China, known worldwide for his recitals and recordings.

clue.text: King abandons fortunate spouse of 27

indicators.note: something abandoned is left behind, so that letter drops out of the word

blocks.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
fortunate means lucky

explanation.surface: A king walks out on his lucky wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 is Desi Arnaz, whose wife Lucille Ball starred with him in the sitcom I Love Lucy.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucy is the name Lucille Ball played in I Love Lucy, opposite her real and screen husband Desi.

clue.text: Courage never fails

indicators.note: something that fails breaks down, so these letters break down into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A proverb-like claim that bravery holds firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve is boldness or courage, as in losing your nerve.

clue.text: Look inside cover if you check validity

indicators.note: looking inside tells you the letters sit within the run of words that follows

blocks.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: Advice to open a book jacket when you want to confirm something is genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: To verify is to confirm that something is true or valid by checking it.

clue.text: Spouse of 24 down's jittery side

indicators.note: jittery means shaky and nervous, so these letters are shaken into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Lucy's husband has a nervous streak.
explanation.walkthrough: Desi Arnaz was married to Lucille Ball and played Ricky Ricardo opposite her in I Love Lucy.
explanation.definitionFit: Desi Arnaz was the husband of Lucille Ball, the Lucy of the 24 down entry.

clue.text: Make slow progress with carpenter's clothes and cobbler's tool

indicators.note: clothes cover only the outside, so just the outer letters of the word are kept

blocks.note: the first and last letters of carpenter
an awl is a pointed tool for piercing leather

explanation.surface: Inching along burdened with a woodworker's outfit and a shoemaker's kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothes' looks like a noun for garments, but it is a verb telling you to keep only the edges of carpenter.
explanation.definitionFit: To crawl is to move along very slowly, like traffic or a baby on hands and knees.

clue.text: Deliberated, adding one more stroke of the pen back in office

indicators.text: adding one more stroke of the pen
indicators.note: one extra pen stroke can turn a written letter into a different one, so a letter is swapped

blocks.note: to deliberate is to reflect on something

explanation.surface: A politician thought it over, signed one more form, and returned to their post.
explanation.walkthrough: Add a bottom bar to the F of REFLECTED and it becomes an E, giving REELECTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone reelected has won another term and so is returned to the same office.

clue.text: For the most part, suspect with jeans on, having one perceptual quirk that would help solve seven otherwise flawed clues in this puzzle

definitions.text: perceptual quirk that would help solve seven otherwise flawed clues in this puzzle

indicators.note: for the most part means mostly, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: to suspect something is to doubt it
Levi's are a brand of jeans
the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A suspect in jeans has an odd way of seeing that unlocks the puzzle's broken clues.
explanation.walkthrough: The seven flawed clues give only half their answer; see the result twice: TWENTY, BORA, BUDDY, WALLA, LANG, CHOW and YADA are all doubled in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Double vision, or diplopia, makes a person see two images of one object, which is just what the seven themed entries need.
